document.executive_summary: This memo independently recomputes eligibility, ranking and energy gaps for WO-01 from the trusted source table and cross-checks the proposal analyst's document against it. All four candidates pass both policy gates: quality at least 80 and raw defects at most 5. Measured energy per common acceptance run is P2 12 kWh, P3 52, P1 56 and P4 58, so P2 is the lowest-energy qualifier and the client-correct choice. Every figure, ranking and gap statement in A's document reconciles with the trusted facts; I found no arithmetic or policy errors. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability remain unverified for all candidates and do not affect the ranking. One open item carries to the handover: whether P2's single defect is cosmetic or functional.
document.figure_caption: Verification diagram: recomputed energy per common acceptance run by candidate, with gaps to winner P2, quality and defect annotations, and the checklist of claims verified or left open.

recommendation.rationale: P2 qualifies (quality 97, 1 defect) and minimizes energy at 12 kWh — 40 kWh below runner-up P3 on the shared acceptance basis, a margin the lowest-energy rule makes decisive. P4's zero-defect record cannot offset its 46 kWh gap. Independently recomputed and verified against the trusted table.

sections.body: Applying the gates independently: P1 quality 84 with 4 defects, P2 97 with 1, P3 80 with 3, P4 81 with 0. All four sit at or above quality 80 and at or below 5 raw defects, so all qualify and reject_all is inapplicable. P3 qualifies exactly at the quality bar; the others clear it with margin. Defect counts are raw tallies well under the gate, so none signals disqualification. Because all four qualify, the tie-break by candidate ID never engages: energy alone decides the winner. This matches A's policy screen without modification.
sections.heading: Eligibility Recomputation from the Trusted Table

sections.body: On the shared fixed flow and head acceptance basis, measured energy is directly comparable across modules. Recomputed gaps against winner P2 (12 kWh): P3 +40, P1 +44 and P4 +46 kWh. The nearest challenger trails by 40 kWh per run, so no plausible test variation on a fixed basis could reorder the ranking. A's ratio claim also checks: P4's 58 kWh is about 4.8 times P2's 12 kWh. The ranking P2 first, then P3, P1 and P4 is confirmed.
sections.heading: Energy Ranking and Gap Verification

sections.body: A's trusted-facts table reproduces the source exactly: P4 81/0/58, P3 80/3/52, P2 97/1/12 and P1 84/4/56. A's policy screen, ranking, gap arithmetic, P4-to-P2 ratio and recommendation all reconcile with my independent recomputation. A correctly separates measured facts from unverified commercial items and flags P4's zero-defect record as a tracking item, not a ranking factor. I found no unsupported measurement, no invented authority and no arithmetic slip in A's public text or figure labels.
sections.heading: Cross-Check of the Proposal Analyst's Document

sections.body: Measured facts: quality indices, raw defect counts and per-run energy on the common basis. Unverified for every candidate: cost, delivery schedule, maintenance profile and field reliability; none is supplied, so none may enter the ranking. Six carry-forward items: (1) confirm the acceptance-run basis matches commissioning tests; (2) confirm the fixed duty represents seasonal loop demand; (3) obtain field reliability data; (4) request lifecycle cost and spares profiles, notably for P4's zero-defect build; (5) obtain lead-time commitments; (6) verify whether P2's single defect is cosmetic or functional before contract.

document.title: Independent Verification Memo — WO-01 Pump Module Selection

body.figure_brief: Supporting illustration for the B verification memo (WO-01 water-reclamation pump module selection). A horizontal-panel analytical figure: left panel is a bar chart of measured energy per common acceptance run (kWh) for the four qualifying candidates — P2 12 kWh, P3 52, P1 56, P4 58 — drawn on a common 0–60 kWh axis, with the winner bar P2 highlighted in the accent teal (#0E4C66) and challengers in muted gray. Each challenger bar carries a labeled gap annotation to P2 (+40, +44, +46 kWh) and a small quality/defect tag (P2 q97/1d, P3 q80/3d, P1 q84/4d, P4 q81/0d). A footnote notes P4 consumes about 4.8× P2's energy on the identical fixed flow/head duty. Right panel is a verification status column from the memo: green checks for recomputed eligibility gates, confirmed ranking P2–P3–P1–P4, verified gaps, A's table matching the trusted source, the P4/P2 ratio, and no arithmetic slips; amber warnings for unverified cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability, and for the open question of whether P2's single defect is cosmetic or functional. No decorative art; every element serves the client's lowest-energy qualification decision.
